name: How does the Denver climate affect tile grout and joint integrity?

mainEntity.name: How does the Denver climate affect tile grout and joint integrity?

acceptedAnswer.text: Denver-area homes experience wide indoor humidity swings between dry winter heating and humid summer weather, causing minor expansion and contraction in wooden subfloors and wall framing. In transition points such as the seam where a tiled wall meets a shower pan or where a floor meets the baseboard, rigid grout frequently cracks under this movement. In communities like Aurora, Centennial, and Parker, contractors use flexible, color-matched silicone caulk at change-of-plane joints instead of grout to absorb shifting without failing or letting water seep behind the tile.
acceptedAnswer.description: Denver's seasonal dry-and-wet cycles cause framing movement, making flexible color-matched caulk essential at corners and wall-floor seams rather than rigid grout.
